verificationHarness.result: 61/61 pass (50 pre-existing + 11 authored for this scan). Every finding below with a poc field is reproduced by a named, passing test.
verificationHarness.caveat: These test files are AUDIT-AUTHORED and are NOT present in lib/antimatter @ 0bb82d8. Never cite them as project test coverage.

findings.title: An ERC20 allowance over ANTIMATTER silently authorises a third party to spend the grantor's STABLECOIN and to keep all of the resulting phUSD
findings.description:
annihilateFrom charges only the antimatter allowance (`_spendAllowance(from, msg.sender, amount)`, :214) but debits TWO of `from`'s assets: `amount` antimatter (:215) and `stableAmount` of `stable` (:222). The stablecoin leg is pulled on Antimatter's OWN standing approval from `from` — an approval `from` must grant to annihilate at all (:191-192, and every front-end will grant it as `type(uint256).max`, exactly as the project's own helper does at test/Annihilation.t.sol:62). No stablecoin allowance to the caller is required or checked. The entire proceeds (~2x) are then sent to `recipient` (:236-237), a caller-chosen address that is validated only against address(0) (:203) and is never required to relate to `from`.

The grantor's exposure is therefore strictly larger than what an ERC20 approval means everywhere else: `approve(bob, N)` on antimatter is, in practice, `approve(bob, N)` on antimatter PLUS `approve(bob, toStableAmount(N))` on every stablecoin the holder has approved to Antimatter, PLUS the right to redirect the output. This is not a bounded grant the approver can reason about from the token they approved.
findings.codeSnippet:
if (from != msg.sender) _spendAllowance(from, msg.sender, amount);  // :214  ANTIMATTER only
_burn(from, amount);                                                // :215
...
IERC20(stable).safeTransferFrom(from, address(this), stableAmount); // :222  from's STABLECOIN, no allowance to msg.sender checked
...
_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount);                                     // :236  caller-chosen recipient
IERC20(address(_phUSD)).safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable);   // :237
findings.attackVector: Alice holds 100 AM and 100 USDC and has approved Antimatter for USDC (mandatory to ever annihilate). Alice grants Bob a routine antimatter allowance of 100 AM — e.g. to a router, an aggregator, an OTC counterparty, or a market that only ever intends to call transferFrom. Bob calls annihilateFrom(usdc, alice, bob, 100e18). Alice loses 100 AM AND 100 USDC and receives nothing; Bob receives 200 phUSD. The delta over the ERC20 baseline (a plain transferFrom, which takes only the 100 AM) is a direct, uncompensated 100 USDC theft. Loss per victim is bounded by min(antimatter allowance, stablecoin approval to Antimatter), which for a max-approved user is the full antimatter allowance.
preconditions: Victim has a non-zero antimatter allowance outstanding to the attacker (a routine, well-understood ERC20 action).
Victim has approved Antimatter to spend a registered stablecoin (mandatory for annihilation; universally a max approval in practice).
findings.invariantViolated: The project's own stated invariant, CLAUDE.md 'Antimatter must never expose a burn outside a completed annihilation' — rationale: 'a holder ... gives up their antimatter and receives nothing at all, with no way to undo it'. That is precisely the state annihilateFrom leaves `from` in whenever msg.sender != from and recipient != from. test_noPublicBurnEntryPoints (test/Annihilation.t.sol:341) trips only on named burn selectors and does not catch this path.
findings.legitimateFlowAnalysis: Neither degree of freedom is individually a problem, and the exploit needs BOTH simultaneously. (a) msg.sender != from with recipient == from is a legitimate keeper/router flow: someone annihilates on your behalf and delivers to you. (b) msg.sender == from with recipient != from is a legitimate donation/routing flow, exercised by test_annihilateToOtherRecipient (test/Annihilation.t.sol:96). Only the conjunction — a third party spending your allowance AND redirecting the output away from you — has no identified legitimate use. Constraining that one combination therefore costs no functionality.
findings.intentionalityNote: The behaviour is asserted as correct by the project's own test_thirdPartySpendsAntimatterAllowance (test/Annihilation.t.sol:130-141), which has `spender` annihilate `user`'s AM and USDC and pay `recipient`. That the behaviour is intended is not a defence: an ERC20 approver has no way to consent to a second asset they were never asked about, and NatSpec at :189-192 carries no suppression authority. Per Law 1 an intended-but-exploitable design is still reportable.
findings.recommendation: Require `recipient == from` whenever `msg.sender != from`. This closes the theft window and preserves both legitimate flows. Alternatives: additionally require `IERC20(stable).allowance(from, msg.sender) >= stableAmount` and spend it, or drop the `from` parameter entirely and make annihilation self-only with a separate recipient.

findings.title: The pairing ratio is taken on trust from the minter's registered `decimals`, and the dangerous direction of a mis-registration fails OPEN and is permissionlessly exploitable
findings.description:
Antimatter's entire economic premise — '100e18 antimatter pairs with 100e6 USDC' (:186) — is computed from `decimals` read out of PhusdStableMinter.stablecoinConfigs (:250), a value the minter's registerStablecoin accepts verbatim and never checks against IERC20Metadata(stablecoin).decimals(). Antimatter performs no independent check either, although it already holds the token address and could do so in one staticcall. The two failure directions are asymmetric:

- decimals OVERSTATED (e.g. 6-dp USDC registered as 18): scale collapses to 1, the pull becomes 1e12x too large, and safeTransferFrom reverts on balance. Fails CLOSED, harmless.
- decimals UNDERSTATED (e.g. 18-dp DOLA registered as 6): scale becomes 1e12, the pull collapses by 1e12x, and BOTH contracts make the same error so it cancels inside calculateMintAmount and nothing reverts. Fails OPEN, silently, at full phUSD issuance.
findings.attackVector: Owner registers an 18-decimal stablecoin with decimals=6 (a single mis-typed argument in registerStablecoin; the two arguments are `exchangeRate, decimals` and neither is validated). From that moment ANY antimatter holder can call annihilateFrom permissionlessly and receive 200 phUSD per 100 AM while surrendering 1e8 raw units (1e-10) of the stablecoin instead of 100. The stable leg of phUSD — the leg that is supposed to be fully collateralised — becomes backed by dust, for as long as the misconfiguration stands and for as much antimatter as exists. There is no revert, no event anomaly, and no on-chain signal; Antimatter's own post-conditions (:230 residue check, :233 non-zero receipt) all pass.
findings.footgunTest: Law 3: a competent, non-malicious owner mis-typing one decimals argument would expect either a revert or a proportionally wrong ratio. They would NOT expect the mistake to be silently absorbed by the mint formula and converted into an unbounded, permissionless free-mint of phUSD. Surprise => footgun => in scope.
findings.rootCauseLocation: The registration-time validation gap is in PhusdStableMinter.registerStablecoin (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:111), a nested submodule excluded at the findings layer. This is filed against Antimatter because (a) Antimatter reads and acts on the value at :250 and defines the pairing ratio that is its own core premise, (b) Antimatter doubles the blast radius by minting a second, uncollateralised phUSD leg on top of the under-collateralised one (:236), and (c) Antimatter can defend itself independently in one line. Flagged for the minter's own audit as well.
findings.recommendation: In toStableAmount, cross-check the registered value: `if (decimals != IERC20Metadata(stable).decimals()) revert DecimalsMismatch(...)` (wrap in a try/catch and fall back to reverting if the token has no decimals()). This makes the dangerous direction fail closed like the safe one already does.

tests: test_M_decimalsUnderstatedIsSilentlyExploitable — 18-dp DOLA registered as 6-dp: 100 AM + 1e8 raw DOLA (1e-10 DOLA) -> 200e18 phUSD, no revert
test_M_decimalsOverstatedFailsClosed — control proving the asymmetry: the harmless direction reverts

findings.title: PhusdStableMinter's daily phUSD issuance cap governs only half the phUSD an annihilation issues; a cap of X permits 2X
findings.description:
PhusdStableMinter enforces a rolling 24h issuance cap denominated in phUSD (maxMintPerDay, lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:215-223) and charges it with `phUSDAmount` — only the phUSD the minter itself mints. Antimatter routes the stable leg through that capped path (:227) but mints the antimatter leg itself, directly on its own FlaxToken authorisation (:236), where the counter cannot see it. At the intended 1:1 exchange rate an annihilation issues `2 * amount` phUSD while consuming only `amount` of the cap. The rail is precisely half the size its operator configured.

This matters more than an ordinary off-by-a-factor because the antimatter leg is the structurally UNCOLLATERALISED half of phUSD (nothing is transferred in for it; its only backing is the antimatter burn at :215), and this cap is the only per-day issuance rail anywhere on the annihilation path. Antimatter itself has no cap of its own, no pause, and mint() (:179) has no supply ceiling.
findings.codeSnippet:
minter.mint(stable, stableAmount);   // :227  charges maxMintPerDay with floor(amount*rate/1e18)
...
_phUSD.mint(recipient, amount);      // :236  charges NOTHING - Antimatter's own FlaxToken authorisation
findings.attackVector: Not an attack so much as a mis-sized control. Operator sets maxMintPerDay(USDC) = 1000e18 intending 'at most 1000 phUSD may enter circulation against USDC per day'. A single annihilation of 1000 AM + 1000 USDC issues 2000e18 phUSD and exactly exhausts the counter, so the operator's monitoring reports the cap as fully used and correctly enforced while twice the intended supply was created. Half of that 2000 is unbacked.
findings.footgunTest: Law 3: a competent, non-malicious operator entering a daily issuance cap would be surprised to learn the effective cap is double the number they typed, and the surprise is invisible — the counter reports 100% utilisation, not 50%. Surprise => footgun => in scope.
findings.rootCauseLocation: The counter lives in the nested minter, but the bypass is created by Antimatter's design decision to mint the second leg itself rather than route it through the capped path. Filed against Antimatter.
findings.severityNote: Honest read: no direct asset loss and no attacker-specific gain, so a downgrade to Low is defensible. Held at Medium because the cap is the only issuance rail on a partly uncollateralised token and it is off by 2x in the unsafe direction, silently.
findings.recommendation: Either mint both legs through PhusdStableMinter so one counter sees the whole issuance, or add an equivalent per-period cap on Antimatter's own leg, or (weakest) rename/document maxMintPerDay as a per-stable DEPOSIT cap so operators size it correctly.

tests: test_M_dailyCapPermitsDoubleTheConfiguredPhUSD — cap 1000e18, single tx issues 2000e18 phUSD, cap then reported exhausted

findings.title: mintedForStable is a balance delta, not an attribution: any phUSD arriving mid-call is forwarded to the caller-chosen recipient
findings.description:
`mintedForStable` is measured as `_phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore` over the window :220-:232 (:232) and forwarded wholesale at :237. It is not compared against what PhusdStableMinter actually minted, which Antimatter could obtain exactly via minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount). Any phUSD that reaches Antimatter during the window is therefore treated as part of the stable leg and paid out to `recipient`. Confirmed reproducible, not theoretical.

The measured-balance pattern is the right instinct on the stablecoin side, where :230's strict equality is what makes the contract fail closed. On the phUSD side the same pattern converts an unexpected inbound into free value instead of a revert. Note the phUSDBefore snapshot at :220 correctly EXCLUDES pre-existing donations — verified by control test — so only the in-window case is affected.
findings.codeSnippet:
uint256 phUSDBefore = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this));                   // :220
... minter.mint(stable, stableAmount); ...                                // :227
uint256 mintedForStable = _phUSD.balanceOf(address(this)) - phUSDBefore; // :232 delta, not attribution
if (mintedForStable == 0) revert PhUSDNotReceived();                     // :233 zero-check only, no upper bound
...
IERC20(address(_phUSD)).safeTransfer(recipient, mintedForStable);        // :237
findings.attackVector: The only non-trusted code that executes inside the window is the stablecoin's own transfer path at :222. A registered `stable` whose transfer hook pushes phUSD to Antimatter causes that phUSD to be swept to the annihilator: PoC injects 500 phUSD from the token's hook and the annihilator walks away with 700e18 instead of 200e18. `stable` must be owner-registered with the minter (:251), which is what holds this to Low — the realistic registered set (USDC, DOLA) has no transfer hooks. The residual concern is a future registration of a hook-bearing or upgradeable stablecoin.
findings.recommendation: Compute the expected stable leg from minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) and use the balance delta only as an equality assertion, so an unexpected inbound reverts rather than paying out.

tests: test_midCallPhUSDInjectionIsForwardedToRecipient — 500e18 injected from the stable's hook; annihilator receives 700e18 (100 AM leg + 100 stable leg + 500 injected)
test_preExistingPhUSDDonationIsNotSwept — control: a pre-call 500e18 donation is correctly excluded and remains stuck (rescueERC20-able)

findings.title: Once phUSD and the minter are both wired, the phUSD address can never be changed — the two setters mutually lock
findings.description:
setPhUSD refuses any address the already-configured minter does not mint (:127-129), and setPhUSDMinter refuses any minter that does not mint the already-configured phUSD (:140-141). PhusdStableMinter.phUSD is `immutable` (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:22), so once a consistent (phUSD, minter) pair is installed there is no ordering of calls that reaches a different phUSD: you cannot change phUSD first (the current minter disagrees) and you cannot install a minter for the new phUSD first (it disagrees with the current phUSD). Neither setter accepts address(0), so there is no way to unwire and start over.

The drift-prevention intent is sound and the mutual check is genuinely valuable. The consequence — that setPhUSD is effectively one-way, and that a phUSD redeployment forces a full Antimatter redeployment (losing all antimatter balances, since Antimatter is non-upgradeable and has no migration path) — is not stated anywhere and is not what a function named `setPhUSD` advertises.
findings.footgunTest: Law 3: an owner reading two independent setters would reasonably believe either can be re-pointed. Discovering the pair is permanently welded only at the moment a phUSD migration is needed is a surprise with an expensive remedy. Surprise => footgun => in scope, at Low because no funds are at risk and phUSD is intended to be permanent.
findings.recommendation: Document the one-way property on setPhUSD, or add an explicit owner-only `rewire(IFlax newPhUSD, PhusdStableMinter newMinter)` that sets both atomically and re-checks consistency, which preserves the no-drift invariant without welding the pair.

findings.title: Antimatter's post-conditions confirm the stablecoin LEFT, never that the yield strategy CREDITED it; on a current-master strategy the stable leg can be minted against principal that was not fully credited
findings.description:
After minter.mint (:227), Antimatter asserts only that its own stablecoin balance returned to stableBefore (:230) and that some phUSD arrived (:233, a non-zero test with no upper or lower bound — the residual behind static finding SA-004). Neither says anything about how much principal the yield strategy actually credited. PhusdStableMinter makes a bare statement call to IYieldStrategy.deposit (lib/phUSD-stable-minter/src/PhusdStableMinter.sol:229) and sizes the phUSD from `amount` (:212/:255), never from what the strategy returned.

On the vault tree the minter is pinned to (043ff2c) deposit returns nothing, so this is internally consistent. On vault master (0110ce4, story-049) deposit returns `creditedPrincipal`, which stories 043/044/048/049 introduce precisely because conservative ERC4626 crediting can credit strictly LESS than `amount`. Solidity ignores surplus returndata so there is no ABI brick, but the shortfall is silently discarded and the stable leg is over-minted relative to the principal actually booked.
findings.parkedReason: PARKED VISIBLY, NOT DROPPED (Law 1: recall beats tidiness). This cannot be adjudicated from the trees available in this audit repo. There is no top-level lib/phUSD-stable-minter or lib/vault sibling; every statement about the minter and the strategy above was read from antimatter's OWN NESTED pins, which are stale by construction (phUSD-stable-minter @ d6ed1156 2026-05-27; its vault @ 043ff2c, a strict ancestor of master). The deployed strategy will be a master-tree build, which this repo does not carry. Per the nested-pin rule, a claim about deployed behaviour must be re-read against the deployed tree.
findings.manualReviewAction: Re-read the DEPLOYED PhusdStableMinter and the deployed yield strategy for the registered stablecoins. If deposit returns creditedPrincipal < amount for any registered stable, size the stable leg from the returned value (a minter-side fix) and/or have Antimatter assert mintedForStable is within tolerance of calculateMintAmount. If the deployed minter is still the 043ff2c-era build, close this as not-applicable.
findings.recommendation: Independently of the above, replace the unbounded `mintedForStable == 0` check at :233 with a two-sided assertion against minter.calculateMintAmount(stable, stableAmount) so a short mint reverts rather than silently shortchanging the annihilator. This also subsumes CODE-004.

findings.title: toStableAmount is a decimals-only rescale and is not a phUSD preview; local `decimals` also shadows ERC20.decimals()
findings.description:
Two QA items on the same function.

(a) toStableAmount is the only public preview on the annihilation path and it ignores exchangeRate entirely (:254-256 use decimals only), while the phUSD actually delivered is `amount + floor(amount * exchangeRate / 1e18)`. At any rate != 1e18 an integrator that derives an expected payout from this function is wrong on the stable leg. Verified: the project's own test_annihilateHonoursMinterExchangeRate (test/Annihilation.t.sol:108-116) sets rate 0.95e18, pulls the full rate-independent 100e6 USDC, and delivers 195e18 rather than 200e18. Note this asymmetry is by design and internally coherent (the stable leg is priced at rate, the antimatter leg always at 1) — it is the ABSENCE of a matching phUSD-side preview that is the QA item. The economic consequence of an unbounded, un-timelocked exchangeRate is econ-scanner territory and is deliberately not adjudicated here.

(b) The local variable `decimals` at :250 shadows the inherited ERC20.decimals()/IERC20Metadata.decimals(). Inside toStableAmount `decimals` means the STABLECOIN's decimals, not this token's — a readability hazard on the single most safety-critical line in the contract (see CODE-002). Corroborates static finding SA-006.
findings.recommendation: (a) Add `previewAnnihilate(address stable, uint256 amount) returns (uint256 stableAmount, uint256 phUSDOut)` that composes minter.calculateMintAmount, and document toStableAmount as the input-side rescale only. (b) Rename the local to `stableDecimals`.

findings.title: recipient is guarded against address(0) but not against address(this); an annihilation can come to rest ON the contract
findings.description: `recipient` is validated only against the zero address (:203). Passing address(this) is accepted: :236 mints `amount` phUSD to Antimatter and :237 transfers mintedForStable from Antimatter to itself, so the full ~2x payout comes to rest on the contract with the antimatter already burned. This is a user footgun rather than a protocol defect — the phUSD is recoverable by the owner via rescueERC20 (:263), and a later annihilation's phUSDBefore snapshot at :220 correctly excludes it so it is not swept to the next annihilator (control-tested). It is nonetheless in tension with the contract's own stated design that 'nothing should ever accumulate here' (:261-262), and address(this) is exactly as cheap to reject as address(0).
findings.recommendation: Add `if (recipient == address(this)) revert RecipientZeroAddress();` (or a dedicated error) alongside the existing check.

tests: test_recipientSelfStrandsPhUSD — 200e18 phUSD settles on the Antimatter contract, antimatter already burned

findings.title: Antimatter has no kill switch of its own; every way to halt annihilation belongs to a different principal
findings.description:
Antimatter is not Pausable and exposes no way for its owner to stop annihilation. Halting it requires one of: PhusdStableMinter's pauser (pause), PhusdStableMinter's owner (setStablecoinEnabled / setMaxMintPerDay), FlaxToken's owner (setMinter / revokeAllMintPrivileges), or the yield strategy's owner (deauthorise the minter as a client / pause the strategy). All four are principals independent of Antimatter.owner(); nothing in any of the contracts requires them to be the same party. If a defect is found in Antimatter itself — including CODE-001 — its own owner cannot stop it, and the fastest lever (FlaxToken.revokeAllMintPrivileges) is global: it silently de-authorises PhusdStableMinter too, emits no per-minter event, and neither contract exposes a view reflecting its own de-authorisation.

This is an operational observation, not a Law-3 'malicious owner' finding: no owner needs to misbehave for the incident-response path to be missing. Filed at QA because the composition is arguably deliberate (Antimatter deliberately keeps no stablecoin list and defers control to the minter), and because a rushed pause on Antimatter would itself add attack surface.
findings.recommendation: Either document the incident-response runbook (who to call, in what order, to stop annihilation) or add an owner-settable `annihilationPaused` flag checked at the top of annihilateFrom, so the contract's own owner holds a proportionate, non-global lever.

reentrancyClassChecklist.evidence: Allowance spend and burn at :214-215 precede the first external call at :219 (CEI verified). annihilateFrom is nonReentrant (:201). The project proves it with a hostile _update-hook token: test/mocks/ReentrantStable.sol + test/Annihilation.t.sol:276.

Call graph is one-directional: Antimatter -> {stable, PhusdStableMinter, FlaxToken}. The minter calls only the yield strategy and FlaxToken; neither holds Antimatter's address nor calls back. Confirmed against the minter source at PhusdStableMinter.sol:226-232 and the strategy interface. The only re-entry vector is the stablecoin's own transfer path at :222, which Antimatter's guard blocks.

The only state-mutating function without nonReentrant is mint() (:179), and it (a) is gated by onlyApprovedMinters so an arbitrary re-enterer cannot reach it, and (b) makes no external call. Even if an approved minter re-entered it mid-annihilation, minting new antimatter cannot alter the in-flight settlement: `amount` was already burned at :215 and both phUSD legs are computed from `amount` and a phUSD balance delta, neither of which reads antimatter supply or balances. rescueERC20 (:263) shares the same guard.

reentrancyClassChecklist.verdict: CLEARED for Antimatter's own views; one transient window parked as MR-01
reentrancyClassChecklist.evidence: Antimatter's external views are balanceOf/totalSupply/allowance (settled at :215, before any external call), toStableAmount (reads only the minter, no Antimatter state), and the approved-minter enumerators (untouched during annihilation). Antimatter holds no share price, exchange rate, NAV, or collateral valuation that an integrator could consume as an oracle. See MR-01 for the one quantity that IS transiently inconsistent.
No ERC721 import, no _safeMint/_safeTransfer, no onERC721Received reference anywhere in src/. Profile property noInboundCallbackHooks, confidence verified.
No ERC1155 import or reference anywhere in src/.

phUSD (FlaxToken) is plain OZ ERC20 with no hooks, so :236-:237 run no callback. A hook-bearing `stable` at :222 is the one inbound-hook surface; it is owner-gated (must be registered with the minter, :251), nonReentrant-blocked for re-entry, and its residual non-reentrancy consequence is filed as CODE-004.

classesCheckedAndCleared.note: Effects (:214-215) strictly precede interactions (:219+). Independently re-verified against source, not taken from the profile.

SafeERC20 used throughout for transfers; forceApprove at :223 and :229 handles the approve-must-be-zero-first requirement, and the allowance is always reset to 0 on the success path (:229) and rolled back on any revert. No standing allowance is left to the minter.
:222 pulls short, the minter's own safeTransferFrom of the full stableAmount then reverts, and the strict residue equality at :230 catches anything that slipped past.

amount==0 (:202), recipient==0 (:203), phUSD==0 (:206/:125), minter==0 (:208/:137/:248), approved minter==0 (:152), rescue to==0 (:264). stable==address(0) fails closed via StablecoinNotRegistered (:251). from==address(0) fails closed on a zero allowance at :214. The one gap is recipient==address(this) — CODE-008.

toStableAmount refuses to round at all: it reverts AmountNotRepresentable (:256) rather than burning antimatter the stable half cannot match. Exactly one truncation exists on the whole path, inside calculateMintAmount, and it rounds toward the protocol. Static finding SA-003 (divide-before-multiply at :255) is a FALSE POSITIVE — the multiply-back is the deliberate exactness round-trip. The residual decimals risk is a wrong REGISTERED value, filed as CODE-002.

Annihilated (:239) reports phUSDAmount as amount + mintedForStable, matching what was actually delivered, and stableAmount in the stablecoin's own decimals as documented at :86. Emitted after all effects. Setter events (:130, :143, :154) all emit previous and new values; setApprovedMinter correctly suppresses the event on a no-op (:153-154).

Unmodified OZ v5.6.1 ERC20; no _update override, no hook, no transfer-tax, no rebase. _spendAllowance at :214 reproduces transferFrom semantics exactly, including the infinite-allowance no-decrement path, and self-annihilation correctly skips it (:214, asserted by test/Annihilation.t.sol:152).
Non-upgradeable: plain constructor at :119, no proxy, no Initializable, no delegatecall anywhere in src/.
grep over src/Antimatter.sol: zero hits for delegatecall, selfdestruct, tx.origin, block.timestamp, blockhash, assembly, unchecked.

manualReviewItems.title: phUSD.totalSupply is transiently inconsistent between the two legs of an annihilation
manualReviewItems.detail: Between :227 (minter mints the stable leg to Antimatter) and :236 (Antimatter mints the antimatter leg to recipient), phUSD.totalSupply reflects one leg of a two-leg issuance while the antimatter it is paired against is already burned. An external protocol reading phUSD supply as a collateralisation input during that window sees an UNDER-count, i.e. it reads the system as better collateralised than it is. Not filed as a finding because (a) the quantity belongs to FlaxToken, not Antimatter, (b) the only way to get execution inside the window is a registered stablecoin's transfer hook at :222, and (c) both legs are increases, so no observer sees an over-count. Re-evaluate if a phUSD collateralisation oracle is ever built, or if a hook-bearing stablecoin is registered.

manualReviewItems.title: Registering phUSD itself as a supported stablecoin
manualReviewItems.detail: Nothing in Antimatter rejects `stable == address(phUSD)`. If the minter's owner ever registered phUSD as its own collateral, :219/:220 would snapshot the same balance twice and the residue check at :230 and the delta at :232 would interfere. Not filed: this is an obviously self-defeating configuration (Law 3, obvious misuse => suppress) and was not reachable in any realistic flow. Recorded so a future reviewer does not have to re-derive it. A one-line `if (stable == address(_phUSD)) revert` would close it cheaply.

manualReviewItems.title: Registered-but-not-approveYS'd stablecoin is a liveness trap Antimatter cannot detect
manualReviewItems.detail: Antimatter's registration test (:251) is `yieldStrategy != address(0)`, which a stablecoin passes as soon as registerStablecoin runs. approveYS (PhusdStableMinter.sol:180) is a SEPARATE owner call, and until it is made every annihilation of that stable reverts inside PhusdStableMinter.sol:229 with no signal Antimatter can surface. Liveness only, no value at risk, and the fix belongs to the minter's registration flow rather than to Antimatter. Recorded as a deployment-runbook item: register and approveYS must be treated as one atomic step.

manualReviewItems.title: Antimatter supply discipline is entirely off-contract
manualReviewItems.detail: mint() (:179) has no supply cap, no schedule and no per-period bound, and every antimatter token is a standing claim on 1e18 of phUSD that nothing collateralises (:236). Solvency of the phUSD system therefore rests on emission discipline enforced outside this contract, by the owner and by whatever contracts sit in _approvedMinters. A bug in ANY approved minter contract converts directly into unbacked phUSD. Explicitly deferred to econ-scanner (incentive/solvency analysis is out of scope for this agent); recorded here so it is not lost between the two.

manualReviewItems.title: Unbounded, un-timelocked exchangeRate reprices every future annihilation
manualReviewItems.detail: The stablecoin PULLED is rate-independent (:254-256, decimals only) while the phUSD MINTED for that leg is rate-scaled, and the antimatter leg is always exactly `amount`. At rate > 1e18 the pair emits more than 2x phUSD per unit of stablecoin taken in; at rate < 1e18 (e.g. a depeg response) the backing ratio of the combined issuance falls. updateExchangeRate (PhusdStableMinter.sol:138-143) is a single owner call with no bound, no sanity check and no timelock, and Antimatter applies no tolerance of its own even though it already reads the config struct at :250. Deferred to econ-scanner as a pricing/incentive question; the code-level half is the missing tolerance assertion, which is covered by the CODE-006 recommendation.

staticFindingReconciliation.note: Independently verified with a passing PoC. Slither's arbitrary-send-erc20 is correct and the allowance-coupling question resolves against the code.

State-after-external-call in setPhUSD/setPhUSDMinter. Both are onlyOwner and the callee is the owner-supplied minter, so a re-entrant exploit needs a malicious owner or a malicious owner-installed minter — Law 3 suppression. The genuine issue in these two functions is the mutual lock, filed separately as CODE-005.
divide-before-multiply at :255-256 IS the exactness round-trip guard that produces AmountNotRepresentable. Removing it would introduce the bug the detector is warning about.
The strict `mintedForStable == 0` check is fine as a zero-test; the real gap is that a short-but-non-zero mint passes unbounded. Also underlies CODE-004.
The 5 discarded tuple fields are genuinely unused. Recorded in classesCheckedAndCleared as an ABI-coupling hazard if the minter's struct is ever reordered.
`decimals` shadowing on the most safety-critical line in the contract.
nonReentrant not first on rescueERC20. Inert: onlyOwner is a pure storage read with no external call, so no re-entry is possible between the modifiers. Style only.
Generic Ownable-surface enumeration. Law 3 — non-malicious owner assumed; no non-obvious footgun in the enumerated setters beyond CODE-005.
Confirmed onlyApprovedMinters gates the only path to _mint: grep of src/Antimatter.sol finds exactly one `_mint(` (:180) and exactly one `_burn(` (:215). No unguarded mint entry point exists.
Magic literals 18/10 in the rescale. Style; the semantic risk at those lines is CODE-002, filed.

summary.note: One High (CODE-001) with a passing PoC and a clean, functionality-preserving mitigation. Both Mediums are Law-3 footguns rather than attacks. Antimatter's reentrancy and settlement engineering is genuinely strong — CEI is correct, the guard is real and regression-tested, and the measured-balance post-conditions make the stablecoin side fail closed. The defects that remain are all at the trust boundary: what Antimatter takes on faith from the minter (CODE-002, CODE-006), what it does not charge against the minter's rail (CODE-003), and what it attributes to the minter without asking (CODE-004).
